captures.description: THE FIVE CASES READ FROM THE SITE, THE THREE PER DIMENSIONS KEPT APART: asked for the arguments of The Apparatus Was the First Summary Layer, grounded in the text, ChatGPT reads it on the Provenance Erasure website's 'Before the Machines' section (chip: Lee Sharks ×9) case by case: the headless treatise, Διονυσίου ἢ Λογγίνου, uncertainty preserved; Sappho 31.17 through Robortello 1554, Bergk 1882, Crusius 1897 and Voigt 1971, PER-D against PER-M; silent re-Aeolicization, the apparatus erasing its own work; survival by quotation, non-carriage as the dominant mode; the white stone of Revelation 2:17, PER 1.0 to everyone and 0 to the receiver, with δυσεξάλειπτος and 22:18–19. It keeps PER-M, PER-C and PER-D as three dimensions, and reads the white stone as the limit at which a magnitude stops telling theft from covenant.

atoms.evidence: Lee Sharks’s “The Apparatus Was the First Summary Layer
“The Apparatus Was the First Summary Layer: Provenance Erasure Before the Machines — Five Cases from the Philological Record, Scored” argues
older editorial apparatuses could erase material while leaving named interventions and stated reasons; modern summary layers can erase at scale without making their decisions equally visible
Sharks treats this as a limit case for the Provenance Erasure Rate (PER).
The text’s central claim is that a critical apparatus—the editorial notes that document textual variants and editorial decisions—can preserve provenance by naming its interventions
argues that the loss of authorship, historical context, and transmission history did not begin with AI
